en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja-Āśāparipūraka, spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was dwelling on Mount Khasarpaṇa, intending to preach the dhāraṇī that dispels all fear.
He was accompanied by immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were Maitreya Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva, Brahmottara Bodhisattva,
Nārāyaṇa Bodhisattva, and so forth, up to Puṇyajñāna Bodhisattva; all of them had received the consecration.
The Great Dharma Prince was also accompanied by a great assembly of Śrāvakas, including Subhūti and others as far as Ānanda, all of whom were great Arhats;
he was further accompanied by immeasurable Brahmā kings, immeasurable sons of gods,
the world-protecting Four Heavenly Kings and their retinues, all humans and non-humans, and even immeasurable men and women.
At that time, from the face of the World-Honored One before the great assembly, he emitted a harmonious light that illuminated the worlds of the ten directions;
the light of the sun, moon, and stars all ceased to appear.

The great earth shook in six ways, and from the heavens there rained down all kinds of precious flowers, which fell everywhere throughout all the celestial palaces, as well as into all the rivers, oceans, spirit palaces, dragon palaces, and the abodes of all honored deities.
The palaces all shook violently, causing unease, and the great assembly conceived a sense of the unprecedented as they gathered for this assembly.
At that time, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the fourfold assembly of śrāvakas from the ten directions came to this gathering.
From the west, there is a buddha-field named Sarvagandhasamudgama; in that land, there is a buddha named Vijaya.
When the Tathāgata Puṣpasaṃkusumitagarbha was fully endowed with the ten titles, there was a bodhisattva named Gaganagañja who rose from among the assembly and asked the Tathāgata:
"By what causes and conditions does this auspicious omen appear? The Buddha said to the bodhisattva Gaganagañja:
"Excellent, excellent! You have asked about this matter at the proper time. From here, passing to the east across eight..."
In worlds as numerous as the sands of ten trillion Ganges Rivers, there is a Buddha-field named the Sahā World.

The sentient beings of that land have come to possess the five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*); it is difficult for the Buddhas of the three periods of time to teach and transform them, and it is difficult even for Bodhisattvas of the tenth stage to do so—how much more so for Bodhisattvas of lower stages who can never benefit them. Yet, in that land, there is a Buddha named...
"Śākyamuni Buddha is now present on Mount Khasarpaṇa before all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the great Śrāvakas, and the assembly of humans and devas, manifesting this auspicious omen.

You should go there to make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and preach the Dharma for the sake of the sentient beings in that land, delivering them from the sea of birth and death and leading them to the shore of Nirvāṇa. At that time, the void...
Upon hearing the Buddha’s words, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.
Together with eight billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, he raised his voice and addressed the Buddha, saying: “Excellent, excellent!
We shall go to that world by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power to make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and to preach the *Abhaya-dhāraṇī* for the sake of the sentient beings in that land.”
At that time, the Tathāgata said to Rāṇi, "Because you are the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Compassionate Ākāśagarbha, whose name is able to fulfill all vows, you may go to that land;
indeed, you may go to that land. Then the World-Honored One extended his right hand, pointed toward the western direction, and spoke these words:
"The Wish-Fulfilling Jewel appears here in the world-system of the West, and its name is One."
In the Sūtra on the Collection of All Fragrances, there is a Buddha named Jñānagarbha Tathāgata.
He has a foremost Bodhisattva named Gaganagañja Bodhisattva who comes and goes to this land desiring to deliver all sentient beings. Thus he comes and goes, manifesting various forms:
he manifests the form of a Śrāvaka, the form of a Pratyekabuddha, the form of a Buddha, and the form of a Bodhisattva.
They manifest in the form of śrāvakas; they manifest in the form of Brahmā kings; they manifest in the form of Śakra; they manifest in the form of Īśvara;
they manifest in the form of Maheśvara; they manifest in the form of celestial generals; they manifest in the form of Vaiśravaṇa;
they manifest in the form of minor kings; they manifest in the form of elders; they manifest in the form of householders; and they manifest in the form of government officials.
They manifest in the form of Brahmins; they manifest in the forms of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs; they manifest in the form of women; they manifest in the forms of boys and girls;

they manifest in the forms of devas, nāgas, and others; they manifest in the form of Vajrapāṇi deities; they manifest in the form of those with the bodhicitta; they manifest in the form of wicked people;
they manifest in the form of those who harmonize with the light; they manifest in forms no different from those of the Buddhas; and they manifest as excellent sons.

He manifests in the form of an excellent teacher; he manifests in the form of a human being; he manifests in the form of a single child; he manifests in the form of birds and beasts; he manifests in the form of the king of medicinal trees;

he manifests in the form of the king of wish-fulfilling jewels; he manifests in the form of one who is gravely ill; he manifests in the form of one who is free from illness; he manifests in the form of the Morning Star.
Thus manifesting in the forms of the thirty-five Buddhas, he travels through various lands according to the needs of sentient beings to deliver and liberate them.
Therefore, all you sentient beings, you should with one mind make offerings to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
This Bodhisattva is able to bestow fearlessness amidst terror and urgent distress; for this reason, this Bodhisattva is named Ākāśagarbha.
Among the eighty thousand great beings, this Bodhisattva is the foremost; among the eight billion bodhisattvas, he is... [foremost].
Because sentient beings do not know the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), this Bodhisattva appears when the stars are visible;

one may perform prostrations while reciting the distinct, elevated tones. Once the prostrations are completed, even those seeking specific attainments will find them fulfilled; how much more so for those who recite, uphold, or transcribe it—they shall swiftly obtain merit and wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, you have granted me permission to speak; World-Honored One, you have granted me permission to speak.
You may speak now; you may speak at once. Then, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, filled with joy, immediately spoke this mantra:
Namo (1) Akāśa (2) Khepaya (3) Oṃ (4) Ari (5) Kā (6) Māri (7) Mūri Svāhā. At that time,
when the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha had spoken this mantra, the great earth shook in six ways, and the celestial Māras [were terrified].
When the non-Buddhists became increasingly uneasy and the bodhisattvas formed the thought that [the Buddha] was heavy, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"You are the mother of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; you are the great field of merit; you are the uninvited teacher for all sentient beings;
you are the physician for those without illness; because you accord with the vows of all sentient beings, you are named 'Able to Fulfill All Vows,' endowed with great kindness and great compassion."
The Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha fulfills the vows of all sentient beings as swiftly as a rapid wind.

If one slanders those who uphold [this teaching], their transgression exceeds the sin of slandering the Buddhas of the three periods of time; how much more so for one who slanders a person who upholds this sutra?

Those who sit upon high seats and do not see those of lower status—those who sit upon high seats shall receive the retribution of sitting atop a mountain of swords. I shall [punish] them for this karmic retribution.
It cannot be fully described; however, for the sake of those who protect and uphold this sutra, he spoke these verses together with me:
"I dispatch eighty thousand great beings, And eight billion bodhisattvas and their like, To always protect and uphold [this sutra]; I dispatch ten rākṣasīs."
I dispatch the Twelve Divine Generals who protect the Dharma, as well as those who shall always provide protection for you;

I dispatch Brahmā and Śakra, and the god Vaiśravaṇa with his twenty-eight divisions, as well as those who shall always provide protection for you; I dispatch both malevolent spirits and benevolent deities.
Even unto the unspeakably many deities, may they always provide protection for those such as me;
I dispatch the Vajrapāṇi Guhyaka spirits, the eight great Nāga Kings,
and the deities of the three lights to always provide protection for those such as me.
When the two World-Honored Ones had finished reciting these verses, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja said, "O two World-Honored Ones, I have already praised you well;

I now join my palms even more reverently. Then eighty thousand great beings and eight billion bodhisattvas spoke with one voice to the Buddha, saying, "For the sake of all sentient beings in the evil world of the future, we shall speak of the fulfillment of all that is sought, just as [the Buddhas] have spoken."

Furthermore, the World-Honored One of that original land said: "Sentient beings of the final dharma who uphold this dhāraṇī should be known for certain as those who uphold the names of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
The World-Honored One further said: "One who upholds this dhāraṇī should be known to surpass the upholding of the names of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Why? Because it is impossible to fully describe all the Buddhas who appear in the world; they are unspeakable."
"To speak exhaustively of the Tathāgatas of our own land and myself would be impossible to finish.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṇyajñāna addressed the Bodhisattva Brahmasikha, saying: 'Beyond these four bodhisattvas, you are the leader.

Can you listen? You are called a Bodhisattva because even after passing through immeasurable kalpas, you cannot exhaust [the virtues of] a Bodhisattva; yet upon hearing my name, you shall become one.'"
Because seeing the essence of me, the Bodhisattva, is equal to and no different from that of a Buddha-Tathāgata, one may invoke my name.
If anyone wishes to be loved and respected by all people, they should recite this mantra thirty-five times every day; its spiritual efficacy will then be clearly manifested.
If it were not so, the cause for awakening would be forever severed, and I would not attain perfect enlightenment. If a person is suffering from illness...
If there are those who spread mats for me but no one asks for them, or those who provide medicine but no one receives it, such that I die of hunger, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.

If a person commits no offense with their mouth yet is suddenly struck by the calamities of kings, and if one who holds this mantra encounters such a person and passes by without saving them, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
If one who holds this mantra encounters someone who has committed an unforgivable transgression and does not escape [the consequences] for them, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
If any impure woman recites this mantra with a sincere mind for twenty-one days, or even up to forty-nine days, she shall be able to transform her female body;
if she does not, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, if one merely holds this mantra, wherever they think of establishing a boundary, even if there are sentient beings of form within it, lions shall not act according to their will.

If I do not take this vow, may I never attain perfect enlightenment. If one who upholds this [teaching] questions those who lack wisdom, or if one fails to teach this sutra to others, they shall forever sever the seeds of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

If one who upholds it desires to achieve *siddhi* within twenty-one days, or even up to forty-nine days, they may fulfill this mantra during the first, fifth, or ninth months; once the calculation of this mantra is complete, it reaches its full measure.
If, after completing one million recitations, there is no attainment of victory, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If anyone who upholds this mantra should fall into the three evil realms, I shall follow them there into those three evil realms. Even for those who lack faith, I shall cause them to reach Bodhi;
even birds and beasts who hear this sutra shall immediately be freed from suffering and anxiety.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying, "What is the name of this sutra?
How should it be titled? The Buddha said, "This sutra is named the *Sutra of the Wish-Fulfilling Gaganagañja*.

It is also named 'The Great Compassion Capable of Fulfilling All Vows,' also named 'The Perfection of Merit and Wisdom,' also named 'The Accomplishment of Siddhi,' also named 'Wish-Fulfilling Satisfaction,' and also named 'Equal toward All.'"

It is also called "Protecting the State and the Clan," also called "The Bright Mirror of Heaven and Earth," also called "Freedom from Illness and Longevity," also called "Inconceivable Vow," also called "Sovereign Perfection and Wish-Fulfillment," also called "Wish-Fulfillment According to Aspiration," also called "The Sovereign Mind of the Dharma Realm," also called "Attaining Dharma-Patience through Recitation," and also called "Attaining Sovereignty through the Sutra."
The mind is thus and so; the various different names of this sutra cannot be fully described.

Because this Bodhisattva Vehicle is the suchness (*tathatā*) of the dharma-nature that transcends all bodhisattvas, it is named the "Space Treasury" (*Gaganagañja*). This Bodhisattva is well able to manifest when the stars appear;
one should prostrate with the five limbs in worship to him. This Bodhisattva’s body is twenty-five *yojanas* in height and appears...
At the time of the true Great Body, you are equal to space and superior to other bodhisattvas; therefore, you are named Ākāśagarbha.

If, while dwelling alone among the assembly in an unfavorable place, you recite this mantra thirty-five times within a single day, yet what you seek is not fulfilled by the following day, may my cause for supreme enlightenment never be accomplished.
Even if it be a woman who has committed an offense, she should hold fast to this mantra.
At the time of death, such a person attains *bodhi* as swiftly as a strong wind blowing away the clouds.
This Bodhisattva’s celestial crown features thirty-five Buddhas, namely:
Śākyamuni Buddha, Vajrāsaṃbheda-kāya Buddha, Ratnaprabhāsa Buddha, Nāgeśvararāja Buddha, Vīrasena Buddha, Vīrarata Buddha, Ratnārcis Buddha, Ratnacandraprabha Buddha, and Abhayadatta Buddha.
Ratnacandra Buddha, Vimala Buddha, Vimalaprabha Buddha, Sūradatta Buddha, Śuddha Buddha, Śuddhadatta Buddha,
Varuṇa Buddha, Varuṇadeva Buddha, Drḍhaśrī Buddha, Candanaśrī Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, Prabhāśrī Buddha,
Amitaketu Buddha, Nārāyaṇa Buddha, Guṇakusuma Buddha, Padmaprabhajñāna Buddha, Jñānaguṇa Buddha.
The Buddha Virtue, the Buddha Merit of Recollection, the Buddha Good Renown of Merit, the Buddha King of Red Flames,
the Buddha Great Victor over Battle, the Buddha Skillful Gait, the Buddha Merit of Universal Adornment, the Buddha Wealth of Merit, the Buddha Jewel Flower Gait,
and the Buddha Merit of the King of Śāla Trees Firmly Abiding on a Precious Lotus— these are the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
The prediction of future Buddhahood is also that which allows a bodhisattva to be designated as a Tathāgata.
Furthermore, in the "Thirty-five Buddhas" practice, paying homage to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha is to pay homage to all Buddhas of the three periods of time and the ten directions.
At that time, the bodhisattvas, the great arhats, bhikṣus, and bhikṣuṇīs joined their palms,
attained the great dhāraṇī of the endurance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and having expressed their joy, paid homage and departed.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-cintāmaṇi-ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
woodblock edition preserved at Kongjōng Seon Temple on the Victorious Peak of Mt. Chōungyo in Sŏseju.
The eleventh month of the fifth year of An'ei, the Bingshen year.
